column1: # selftest-cache-inputs.tsv — the OPT-IN declaration table for the selftest pass cache.
# A suite with a row here participates in tools/run-selftests.sh's content-addressed pass
# cache: when the sha256 of (epoch, OS, bash major, suite path, the git blob id of every
# declared input) is already recorded as a pass on this lane, the suite is not re-run.
# A suite with NO row is ALWAYS RUN. That is the whole safety posture: under-declaring a
# suite's inputs produces a silently-skipped gate, which is the cardinal failure mode in this
# repo, so participation is opt-in and only the rows below carry the risk.
# TAB-separated. Columns:
#   suite repo-relative path <TAB> input repo-relative path
# ONE INPUT PER ROW, so adding one is a one-line diff. An input may name a file or a
# DIRECTORY; a directory contributes every regular file beneath it, in sorted order.
# THE RUNNER REJECTS, with rc=2 and a named error, a table that:
#   - names a suite it did not discover, or an input that does not exist (stale row);
#   - omits the suite ITSELF from its own input set — no suite may cache past an edit to its
#     own bytes;
#   - omits the script under test, where that script is the suite's `<stem>.sh` sibling;
#   - declares nothing besides the suite itself.
# The table is validated on EVERY sweep, including one running with no cache at all, so a
# malformed declaration reds locally rather than waiting for CI to read it.
# WHAT BELONGS HERE. Only suites whose cost is worth the declaration burden. Cost is measured
# in tools/selftest-suite-timings.tsv. A suite whose composed set IS its transitive closure
# cannot be enumerated stably from the suite and is DROPPED. Directory rows cannot express a
# set like that either when its universe is the TRACKED set, while a directory row contributes
# every regular file beneath it, untracked included.
# Dropping a row is always safe: the suite simply always runs.
# EVERY SET MUST BE DERIVED FROM THE SUITE, not copied from a ticket. A suite typically
# reads more than an eyeball would list — exactly the under-declaration the self-inclusion
# rule cannot catch.
# AND THE SET IS THE TRANSITIVE CLOSURE, not the files the suite names. Neither of the rules
# above can reach depth 2: a suite whose own path and whose subject are both declared still
# under-declares if that SUBJECT resolves a third file at run time (claim-issue.sh, for one,
# resolves gh-bot.sh beside itself). When you add a row, follow every variable-rooted
# resolution out of every declared script until it terminates, and record where it terminated.
# The next block is how you enumerate them.
# DERIVE THAT MECHANICALLY, AND OVER PATHS RATHER THAN OVER SCRIPTS. Grep each declared script
# for the paths it BUILDS FROM A VARIABLE, and match every one against the rows below. Three
# things a prose reading misses.
#   (1) A resolution may target a .md or a .tsv as readily as a .sh, so a sweep scoped to
#       `*.sh` mentions can be accurate and still incomplete.
#   (2) A target the subject only tests for EXISTENCE is an input too: its absence flips the
#       suite's verdict, while the key — content-addressed over the DECLARED rows alone — does
#       not move, which is a stale pass.
#   (3) TWO ROOTS, and they answer differently. A ${BASH_SOURCE[0]}- or $0-rooted path names a
#       file shipped BESIDE the subject, and is an input whenever the subject reaches it. A path
#       rooted at the GRADED TREE ($REPO_ROOT, `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`) is an input only
#       if the suite runs the subject against a tree that HAS the file — under a mktemp fixture
#       it usually does not, and the case is asserting the absent branch. Classify each; do not
#       assume either answer.
# No suite opts in today: every suite is always run.
